## Closing the Loop

- Every habit in this series has been building toward one idea: your work should be usable by someone who isn't you.
- Today: AI-assisted code, packaging your project for deposit, and what reproducibility actually asks of you.

## AI Can Write Code — Who Checks It?

::: {.incremental}
- AI-generated code can run without error and still be wrong — statistically, biologically, or just quietly.
- Everything you've learned (functions, error messages, Git history, `renv.lock`) is exactly the toolkit for verifying code you didn't write yourself.
- The habits don't change. Only who typed the first draft does.
:::

## Series Wrap-Up

- The repo is the reproducible artifact — whether you wrote every line of it or not.
- Code, environment, and data now travel together, with a record of how they got that way.
